economy.summary: Supports raising Pennsylvania's minimum wage to $15 per hour and indexing it to inflation, saying no wage that puts a full-time worker under the poverty level should be acceptable.
economy.short: Supports $15 minimum wage indexed to inflation.

taxes.summary: Said the completed 2025-26 state budget contained much to celebrate, citing public school funding increases and a new tax credit she said benefits nearly 1 million Pennsylvanians, while criticizing Senate Republican leaders for taking over 134 days to finish it.
taxes.short: Praised 2025 budget's school funding, tax credit; criticized delay.

abortion.summary: Her campaign site says she will fight to enshrine protections for a safe, legal abortion unencumbered by government interference into Pennsylvania law, and that she supports comprehensive sexual education.
abortion.short: Supports enshrining legal abortion protections into Pennsylvania law.

education.summary: Advocates increasing state funding for K-12 public schools and opposes directing taxpayer dollars to what she calls failing cyber charter schools, saying resources should go to classrooms instead.
education.short: Supports more K-12 funding; opposes cyber charter subsidies.

healthcare.summary: Supports expanding healthcare access for all Pennsylvanians, protecting Affordable Care Act provisions, closing corporate tax loopholes to fund care, and lowering prescription drug prices.
healthcare.short: Supports expanding access, protecting ACA, lowering drug prices.

energy.summary: Opposed HB 1100, a bill she said would provide nearly one billion dollars in subsidies to petrochemical companies, and supports transitioning to clean, renewable energy while protecting workers affected by the transition.
energy.short: Supports renewable energy transition; opposed petrochemical subsidies.

guns.summary: In the 2025-2026 legislative session she co-sponsored House Bill 837, which would limit handgun purchases and establish a Violence Prevention Account.
guns.short: Co-sponsored bill limiting handgun purchases, creating violence-prevention account.

economy.summary: Told WESA he entered the race to address what he sees as failed policies resulting in seniors and others losing their homes and rising prices of utilities and gas, and describes his campaign focus as affordability, accountability, improvement, and reform.
economy.short: Cites rising utility, gas prices; focuses on affordability, reform.
